1. Aim for a consistent earlier bedtime, ideally before midnight, to increase total sleep duration toward 7-9 hours per night, as late nights (after midnight) are strongly linked to insufficient sleep and lower sleep quality.

7. Incorporate regular moderate exercise during the day (but not within 2-3 hours of bedtime) to promote deeper sleep and reduce stress, which may help lower the frequency of palpitations.
8. Practice stress-reduction techniques such as meditation, deep breathing, or progressive muscle relaxation before bed, as emotional stress can contribute to both insomnia and heart palpitations.
9. Since palpitations almost exclusively occurred with sleep scores ≤45 and durations ≤310 minutes, treat these as critical thresholds; prioritize actions to keep sleep duration above 5-6 hours and quality high.
10. Consult a healthcare provider for a clinical sleep evaluation, given the rare sleep apnea occurrences and their association with extremely poor sleep, to rule out sleep-disordered breathing that may worsen cardiac risks.
11. Discuss the documented atrial fibrillation and premature heartbeats with a cardiologist, as the bidirectional relationship between poor sleep and arrhythmias may require targeted medical management.
12. Keep a sleep and symptom diary to track bedtime, wake time, sleep quality, and any palpitations, helping you identify personal triggers and monitor improvements over time.
